label: Late copy phase, approaching an upcoming y/q output
explanation: Fires only in the copy phase (t > L; zero on original and delimiter steps), almost entirely at absolute steps t >= 10, so mostly in long sequences (L = 8-9 hold 87% of the mass), with the rate highest at t = 12 and t = 17. It never fires on the first occurrence of a token. Within the copy phase it is token-modulated: rate and mass are highest when y (5.5x lift) or q (3.7x lift) is being output now or in the next few steps. The strongest examples ramp up over 2-4 copy steps before a y/q output and peak about 1-2 steps before it. Weaker lifts also show up for s, l, v, a, k as current or next outputs. Requiring t >= 10 and a y/q output within the next 0-4 steps gives about 0.48 precision and 0.43 recall (0.54 mass recall) on dev. Widening the token set to y,q,s,l,a,k raises mass recall to 0.79 but lowers precision to 0.33. Much activation is diffuse, low-magnitude firing across mid/late copy steps that no simple token condition captures.

scorecard.summary: Graded preference over the next token to output (most: y, q, a, k, s, l; least: j, o, f, z) and the token being output, by phase (copy phase: y, q, s, l; input phase: ; delimiter step: ); timing cues that raise it most: phase=2, L=9, t=12.
